clue.text: Defects turning up in quick ones

definitions.meaning: read as two words, arrivals that are brief or quick

explanation.surface: Faults keep appearing in hurried efforts.
explanation.definitionFit: Failings or deficiencies are flaws, exactly what defects are.

clue.text: The main drink where there's a harbour bar

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the open ocean
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: Ocean and a glass of fortified wine where a harbour has a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harbour bar' suggests a pub on the quay; here it is a sandbank at a harbour mouth, the mark of a coastal town with docks.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal town with docks is the kind of place that has a harbour and its bar.

clue.text: Stupefied a dope, it may be

indicators.note: says the letters of the preceding words may be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Someone dazed after taking a drug, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' tells you to rearrange A, DOPE and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Drugged with a narcotic leaves someone dulled and stupefied.

clue.text: Gently stimulate a bird, badly fed

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
ill can mean badly, as in ill-treated
ate means fed, took food

explanation.surface: Tease a bird that has been poorly fed.
explanation.definitionFit: To excite or arouse mildly, as with tickling, is to stimulate gently.

clue.text: Eyeball — it's sphere of action

definitions.meaning: the eye socket or the eye itself, an old sense
a range of activity or influence

explanation.surface: An eye is its own field of operation.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the eye's bony socket or the eye itself, and a field of influence or activity.

clue.text: Put on a pedestal, one is in woeful state

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: says the word is goes inside the word for a woeful state

parts.note: dole is an archaic word for grief or sorrow
taken as written

explanation.surface: Admiring someone excessively, one ends up miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: DOLE here is the old word for sorrow, not unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: To worship or revere someone is to place them on a pedestal, an idiom.

clue.text: Yellow resin from quarry containing spongy ground

indicators.note: the word for quarry holds the word for spongy ground inside it

parts.note: game is hunted animals, the hunter's quarry
a bog is wet, spongy ground

explanation.surface: A yellow gum dug out of a pit with marshy soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarry' suggests a stone pit; it is prey, GAME.
explanation.definitionFit: This gum-resin from Asian trees is used as a yellow pigment.

clue.text: Early bathers change for driving test

indicators.note: says the letters of the two words are changed around into a new order

explanation.surface: Early-morning swimmers swap for a road exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' asks you to rearrange EARLY BATHERS.
explanation.definitionFit: The roadside device that measures alcohol on a motorist's breath is a test given to drivers.

clue.text: Note a desire — a practical one

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
list is an archaic word for wish or desire

explanation.surface: Writing down a wish is the act of a sensible person.
explanation.walkthrough: LIST as desire is old-fashioned (compare listless, lacking desire).
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pragmatic who sees things as they are is a practical person.

clue.text: Female fashion pioneer found in bed

definitions.meaning: Amelia ..., American campaigner for loose trousers for women
a flowering plant in a flower bed

explanation.surface: A woman who led fashion was discovered between the sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: Amelia Bloomer gave her name to baggy trousers; a plant that flowers grows in a garden plot.

clue.text: Put in duty-list when overweight? Here's a tablet

indicators.note: says the word for put goes into the word for a duty-list

parts.note: a rota is a roster of duties
set means put or placed
a stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds, and in this down clue it sits below what precedes it

explanation.surface: Being too heavy, someone is added to the work roster; here is a pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overweight' splits as 'over weight': the first part lies above STONE, a British unit of 14 pounds, in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The inscribed slab that unlocked hieroglyphs is a famous stone tablet in the British Museum.

clue.text: Marginal note after being in trouble

indicators.note: says the word for after is placed inside the word for trouble

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
post means after, as in post-war

explanation.surface: A note in the margin once things went wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: An annotation written in a margin is the old meaning of this word for a side note.

clue.text: Sea deities are said to be hackneyed ones

indicators.note: points to how the phrase sounds when spoken

parts.note: trite ones are hackneyed, overused ones

explanation.surface: Gods of the ocean are considered clichéd.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Triton and his kind were mermen gods of the sea.

clue.text: Death can be extremely unpopular

indicators.note: says the letters of the word before can be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Dying can be very much disliked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' asks you to rearrange DEATH.
explanation.definitionFit: Something loathed is thoroughly disliked, extremely unpopular.

clue.text: Harmony provided by people in a welcome

indicators.note: says the word for people goes inside the word for welcome

parts.note: to greet is to welcome
men means people

explanation.surface: Concord is supplied by those offering a warm reception.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in accord, holding the same view, is a state of harmony.

clue.text: Plastering, by interpretation

definitions.meaning: a coat of plaster on a wall
a performance or version of a piece

explanation.surface: Coating walls, according to one reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a coat of plaster on brick and a performer's version of a work.

clue.text: Alice and love could be lukewarm

indicators.note: says the letters gathered could be rearranged into a new word

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Alice and her romance might be only half-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' asks you to rearrange ALICE, AND and O (love).
explanation.definitionFit: The Laodicean church was rebuked in Revelation for being neither hot nor cold, so the word means half-hearted.

clue.text: It's tedious. Open the wine

parts.note: ope is an archaic, poetic form of open
rosé is a pink wine

explanation.surface: A dull business: uncork the bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Laborious, toilsome work is wearisome and tedious.

clue.text: He urges us in taking a preliminary shot, say

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: signals that a word should be heard as it sounds

parts.note: a sighter is a trial shot in target shooting to check aim

explanation.surface: Someone encourages us while having a warm-up shot.
explanation.walkthrough: A sighter is a practice shot in target shooting, used to check the sights.
explanation.definitionFit: One who goads or stirs others to act is someone who urges them on.

clue.text: Short break for the butterfly

definitions.meaning: a punctuation mark giving a brief pause
a British butterfly with ragged wings and a white ...-shaped mark

explanation.surface: A brief holiday for an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation mark marks a brief pause, and a British butterfly is named for its white mark.

clue.text: The fortress in novel sort of dialect

indicators.note: a novel kind of the word means its letters made new, rearranged

explanation.surface: A stronghold appears in a new kind of regional speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel sort of' asks you to rearrange DIALECT.
explanation.definitionFit: A stronghold guarding a city is its fortress.

clue.text: Average notices we hear for The Bacchantes

indicators.note: signals the phrase is heard, not read

parts.note: mean is average and ads are notices

explanation.surface: Middling reviews for a classical drama.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bacchantes is a play by Euripides about frenzied female followers of Bacchus, which makes the reviews surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenzied female worshippers of Dionysus, also called Bacchae, are the Bacchantes.

clue.text: Sail in a coat

definitions.meaning: a fore-and-aft trysail on a ship

explanation.surface: Going to sea wearing a jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a ship's trysail and a short jacket named after an Earl Spencer.

clue.text: Salient field-work in severe danger

indicators.note: says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A projecting earthwork under grave threat.
explanation.definitionFit: A V-shaped earthwork pointing toward the enemy is a salient fortification.

clue.text: Beg to negotiate in French originally

parts.note: en is French for in
to treat is to negotiate, as in treat with the enemy

explanation.surface: Asking to bargain in French at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore or plead earnestly is to beg.

clue.text: Stuck around — son got ready to sleep

indicators.note: says the word for stuck goes around the letter for son

parts.note: rooted means stuck fast in place

explanation.surface: Lingered about until the boy was ready for bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuck around' reads as a phrase meaning lingered; split it into the word and its indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds settle on a perch for the night, which is getting ready to sleep.

clue.text: Aloof in drag in the pub

indicators.note: says the word for drag is put inside the word for the pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
to draw is to drag or pull

explanation.surface: Someone standoffish turns up cross-dressed at the local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drag' suggests cross-dressing; it means pull, DRAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Withdrawn into oneself, a reserved person is distant and aloof.

clue.text: Woman's halo deceives the birds

parts.note: her means belonging to a woman
a halo is a ring of light
to gull is to deceive or dupe

explanation.surface: A lady's saintly glow fools people.
explanation.definitionFit: These large grey-backed seabirds are a common species of gull.
